subject: four-eyed fish
title: This Fish Sees Above and Below the Water at the Same Time, With Two Eyes

scenes.text: This fish watches the sky and the river at the same time.
It's called the four-eyed fish, but it only has two eyes. Each one is split in half.
A band of tissue divides every eye into a top half and a bottom half, each with its own pupil.
It swims with the waterline running exactly across the middle of its eyes.
The top half is built for air and the bottom for water, so the lens is thicker in one direction to correct the focus.
Birds above, fish below, and it sees both in focus. From the mouth of the Amazon to Trinidad.

description:
This fish watches the sky and the river at the same time.
The four-eyed fish (Anableps) of Central and South American estuaries has only two eyes, but each is divided by a band of tissue into an upper and a lower half with its own pupil and cornea. It cruises with the waterline across the middle of its eyes. The upper half is adapted for vision in air, the lower for water, and the lens changes thickness from top to bottom to correct for the two media, so predators above and prey below both stay in focus.
What would you do with a split-screen view of the world?
first_comment: Bonus: they are live-bearers whose sex organs sit on the left or right side, so a right-sided male can only mate with a left-sided female. Which animal has the strangest eyes?
